content:
Let \(c\) be the chord length of an arc and \(s\) its sagitta (the maximum distance from the chord to the arc). The circle’s radius is

\[
r=\frac{(c/2)^2+s^2}{2s}.
\]

Using the common scale of the diagram, the approximate measurements are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
\text{Arc} & c & s & r\\ \hline
R & 220 & 64 & 127\\
A & 255 & 128 & 128\\
B & 164 & 47 & 95\\
C & 226 & 47 & 159
\end{array}
\]

Thus Arc A has essentially the same radius as Arc R.

\[
\boxed{\text{A: Arc A}}
\]
